newsitem.title: USA: Miami airport cargo up 1.5 percent in January.
newsitem.headline: Miami airport cargo up 1.5 percent in January.

text.p: Cargo traffic at Miami Interantional Airport was up a modest 1.5 percent in January, according to statistics released by the Dade County Aviation Department.
"They were essentially flat and February will also be be pretty flat," Peter Reaveley, MIA's director of route development said Monday.

"The second half of this year will be incredible," Reaveley said. He explained that traffic will be strong due to new bilateral aviation agreements and import demand in South America because of privatization efforts.
All cargo, including mail, amounted to 141,074 tons in January. Of that 113,367 tons was international cargo. International was up 3.18 percent from the same month of 1995.
Domestic cargo including mail was down 4.78 percent to 27,708 tons in January, according to the Dade County statistics.
